merger_name: AerFin - acquisition of aircraft from Qantas

anzsic_codes.name: Other Machinery and Equipment Wholesaling n.e.c.

merger_description:
AerFin Limited (**AerFin**) proposes to acquire Boeing 737-838 aircraft and engines from Qantas Airways Limited (**Qantas**), with delivery of each individual aircraft and engines due to take place progressively from October 2026 to May 2033 as the aircraft are retired by Qantas (the **Acquisition**).

AerFin is a UK-headquartered global aviation services company specialising in aftermarket material supply (referred to as used serviceable material (**USM**)), aircraft and engine trading, and nose-to-tail component support solutions. AerFin buys, sells, leases and repairs aircraft, engines and parts. AerFin generally targets mid-life and end-of-life commercial aircraft and engines (typically 8-15 years old) and monetises them principally through teardown, repair and sale of USM, and from time to time through whole-asset sales, short-term leasing of engines or other high value parts and related support programmes. AerFin's customers are airlines, aircraft lessors and aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul organisations. While AerFin does make some USM sales to customers in Australia, AerFin does not have a physical presence in Australia.

Qantas is an Australian-based domestic and international airline. Qantas also operates airline-related businesses including freight operations and loyalty programs, and various airline subsidiaries, namely Jetstar Airways Pty Limited (which operates domestic and international flights), regional airline QantasLink and Network Aviation.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the Acquisition represents a small proportion of the total
global supply of retired commercial aircraft
b. there are alternative suppliers and acquirers of aircraft and
component parts globally.
• In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
